items.title: Open v2.77.0: move the changelog history out of the index into standards/CHANGELOG.md; fix the changelog typos, the order and the footer stamp
items.spec:
Owner ruling for this run (OWNER_SCOPE item 1 puts WAS-R-03 in scope; the session lead decides C-02): the changelog moves. Release number is v2.77.0 (minor: the amendment process changes), and this is the ONE standard version the whole run produces; every later WS item appends a bullet to the v2.77.0 entry instead of bumping again.
End state:
- New standards/CHANGELOG.md: a short header ('# Ka0s WoW Addon Standard: changelog', one sentence saying the index carries only the current entry and this file carries every earlier one, newest first), then the 99 entries currently at standards/STANDARDS.md:99-253 (v2.76.1 .. v1.0.0) moved verbatim, with exactly three edits: (a) the v2.19.0 entry sits above v2.18.0 (today it is at :218 between v2.17.1 and v2.17.0; WAS-A-18); (b) the v2.6x entry at old :120 reads 'preview-mode' not 'preview-mode-§' (WAS-R-12 / WAS-A-13); (c) old :168 reads 'automated-tests-§3' not 'automated-tests-§?' (WAS-A-13). The name is CHANGELOG.md: it is not at a repo root, so documentation-§1/§3's addon-root ban does not reach it (say so in one clause in CLAUDE.md).
- standards/STANDARDS.md: title becomes '(v2.77.0, <landing date>)'. '## Changelog' keeps only the new v2.77.0 entry (lead sentence: the 2026-10-07 review-and-audit remediation; first bullet: the changelog moved and why, with the 418,659 -> ~36 KB index measurement) followed by the line 'Full history: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).' CHANGELOG.md is listed under '## Related documents' and NOT under '## Sections' (tools follow Sections; history is not normative). The footer drops its date: '**End of index. The normative rules live in the section files linked above.**' (WAS-R-07: the header is the single authority).
- Version stamps rolled to v2.77.0: README.md:160 Status, standards/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md:11, standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md:1, CLAUDE.md:143 ('As of v2.77.0').
- Process wording rewritten to the new home: CLAUDE.md:82-84 (index carries front matter, reading guide, Sections, Related documents and the CURRENT changelog entry; on the next release the previous entry moves to the top of standards/CHANGELOG.md) and :135; standards/README.md:13 (drop 'at its top'), :32 and :63-64; README.md:82 (section A step 4); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Module Map and Documentation map gain a standards/CHANGELOG.md row.
- documentation.md:259 (Tier 1 data-flow row): 'documentation-§1 item 8' -> 'documentation-§1 item 6' (the live half of WAS-A-13; item 6 is '## How <it> works').
- Cross-repo handoff H-01 (owned by the dev-copilot planner, not this item): dev-copilot commands/wow-harvest-standards.md:152 and agents/wow-standards-audit.md:108 must point at standards/CHANGELOG.md / the current-entry-in-index shape; that dev-copilot item depends on WS-01 and lands in the same merge, so no build ever sees one without the other.
items.steps:
1. Record the before size: wc -c standards/STANDARDS.md (expect 418659).
2. Extract lines 99-253 into standards/CHANGELOG.md under the header; move the v2.19.0 line above v2.18.0; apply the two typo fixes.
3. Replace STANDARDS.md ## Changelog with the v2.77.0 entry + 'Full history' pointer; add the Related-documents bullet; strip the footer date; bump the title.
4. Roll the four other version stamps; rewrite the CLAUDE.md / standards/README.md / README.md / ARCHITECTURE.md process wording; fix documentation.md:259.
5. Prove the move is lossless (verify block), then commit 'WS-01: open v2.77.0; changelog history moves to standards/CHANGELOG.md'.
items.verify:
cd ../WowAddonStandards
wc -c standards/STANDARDS.md   # < 60000
grep -c '^- \*\*v' standards/CHANGELOG.md   # 99
grep -c '^- \*\*v' standards/STANDARDS.md   # 1 (v2.77.0)
git show HEAD~1:standards/STANDARDS.md | sed -n '99,253p' | grep '^- \*\*v' | sed 's/preview-mode-§/preview-mode/;s/automated-tests-§?/automated-tests-§3/' | sort > /tmp/a; grep '^- \*\*v' standards/CHANGELOG.md | sort > /tmp/b; diff /tmp/a /tmp/b   # empty
grep -n '^- \*\*v2\.1[789]' standards/CHANGELOG.md   # order v2.19.0, v2.18.0, v2.17.1, v2.17.0
grep -n 'preview-mode-§\|automated-tests-§?\|Authoritative as of' standards/   -r   # nothing
git grep -n 'v2\.76\.1' -- CLAUDE.md README.md standards/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md   # nothing
grep -n 'documentation-§1 item 8' standards/standards/documentation.md   # nothing
tr -dc '\r' < standards/CHANGELOG.md | wc -c   # 0

items.title: This repo keeps its own docs/audits/ and docs/reviews/ stores: rewrite the self-description, register both stores, drop the file count and single-source the roster
items.spec:
The 2026-10-07 audit and review bundles are already committed (RA-00, 63ccc5c). documentation-§8 applies audit-review-history unchanged to a documentation-and-tooling repo, so this repo's prose must stop forbidding them.
- Rewrite CLAUDE.md:11-15 ('This repo does not run audits'), :61-62 ('Audit and review runs are not in this repo') and :107-110 ('Audits are per-repo and frozen ... never here'); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:23-24; README.md:17-18 and :154-155. New sense everywhere: an addon audits itself in its own repo; this repo, being audited too (ADDONS.md documentation-and-tooling table, documentation-§8), keeps its OWN documentation-lane docs/audits/<YYYY-MM-DD>/ and docs/reviews/<YYYY-MM-DD>/ frozen stores (audit-review-history), never edited after the fact. AUDIT.md:3-6, standards/README.md:5-6 and ADDONS.md:5-7/:80-81 are accurate (they are about addon audits) and stay as they are apart from an optional one-clause qualifier.
- CLAUDE.md Layout tree gains 'docs/audits/' and 'docs/reviews/' lines.
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md '## Documentation map' (:69): one directory row each for docs/audits/<date>/ and docs/reviews/<date>/ as frozen stores, modelled on the harvests/<date>/ row (documentation-§3 names frozen stores once as directories).
- DEPENDENCIES.md:14: drop '67 tracked files: 63 Markdown'; restate by kind: 'Markdown only, plus LICENSE, .gitattributes and two logo images' (and, once WS-10 lands, that item adds the script).
- WAS-A-17: README.md:47-49 drops the eleven names and the count and links standards/ADDONS.md; line-endings.md:72-74 replaces the enumeration with 'every addon in ADDONS.md, plus LibKa0s' (CLAUDE.md:78 convention).
- WAS-R-11: standards/ADDONS.md Folder column becomes plain code text (`../../AbsorbTracker/`, no link wrapper) on all 11 addon rows plus the LibKa0s and dev-copilot rows; :16's 'local sibling paths' note stays.
- Changelog: one bullet appended to the v2.77.0 entry.
items.steps:
1. grep the cited passages; rewrite each in place.
2. Add the two map rows and the Layout lines; restate DEPENDENCIES.md:14.
3. Replace the two roster enumerations with ADDONS.md pointers; unwrap the Folder links.
4. Append the changelog bullet; commit 'WS-02: ...'.

items.title: toc-file-§5: the load-bearing denominator covers every position in the listing; AUDIT.md step 4 checks the whole TOC; the worked example is cited by heading
items.spec:
Root cause of cluster C05 (AT-A-04/05, CM-A-03, LH-A-01/15..18 are addon items that cite this one).
- standards/standards/toc-file.md denominator paragraph (~:154-157, 'The denominator this MUST is measured against'): load-bearing positions are established by reading EVERY listed file that binds, reads or writes an NS member (or a library major) at file scope — in modules\ and settings\ as much as *Setup.lua and core\Constants.lua — not only the seam files. Keep the 'not by counting lines' point and the 2026-09-07 history paragraph.
- Add one sentence: a load-bearing constraint may be 'below at least one of X/Y/Z' (LH-A-15 shape); the comment names what resolves, not a single file, when several satisfy it.
- AUDIT.md step 4 'Check the TOC's position annotations (toc-file-§5)' (~:402): 'In the # Core block, every line' -> 'At every position in the listing (# Core, # Defaults, # Modules, # Settings and any other group), every line'; 'Read the seam files (*Setup.lua) and core/Constants.lua' -> 'Read every listed file for file-scope reads/writes of NS members and library majors'.
- toc-file.md:171 worked example (AT-A-14): replace 'AbsorbTracker.toc:35-42' with the block's heading, '# Core (the LibKa0s-Env seam loads first)' in AbsorbTracker.toc (the block actually spans :37-44 today, which is why a line range is the wrong form).
- Changelog bullet appended to v2.77.0 (a clarification of an existing MUST's denominator, no new obligation).
items.steps:
1. Edit toc-file.md denominator paragraph and worked-example citation.
2. Edit AUDIT.md step 4 to match.
3. Append changelog bullet; commit.

items.title: documentation-§3/§6/§8 and library-stack-§7 agree with themselves: §6 cites §3's frozen-store list, §8's arithmetic and single executable-content trigger, the documentation-§5/§6 row labels, ordinals and Tier 2 membership
items.spec:
All in standards/standards/documentation.md unless noted.
- WAS-A-14 (§6 'Frozen bundles are exempt', ~:625-636): delete the private four-store list; cite documentation-§3's frozen/generated list by reference (docs/audits/, docs/reviews/, docs/automated-tests/<run>/, docs/perf-analysis/<run>/, docs/revendor/<date>-v<tag>/, docs/superpowers/, docs/investigations/). Narrow the automated-tests exemption to docs/automated-tests/<run>/ (README.md and RESULTS.md are live). Add a clause for a repo's own frozen stores (this repo's harvests/ and standards/_raw/; a library's equivalents). Replace the grep --exclude-dir sweep with a git ls-files pipeline that excludes every frozen store, e.g. git ls-files -z -- '*.md' ':!:docs/audits/**' ':!:docs/reviews/**' ':!:docs/automated-tests/*/**' ':!:docs/perf-analysis/*/**' ':!:docs/revendor/*/**' ':!:docs/superpowers/**' ':!:docs/investigations/**' ':!:libs/**' ':!:tests/_kit/**' ':!:harvests/**' ':!:standards/_raw/**' | xargs -0 grep -nE '§[0-9]+\.[0-9]' (keeping the 'command, not enumeration' reporting rule).
- WAS-A-12: drop the ordinals at :170 ('the ninth mandated section') and :347 ('the tenth ARCHITECTURE.md section'); refer to the sections by name.
- WAS-A-15 + DC-A-15 (§8): fix the arithmetic at ~:698 so Module Map is counted once (five sections dropped, five kept, one of the five — Module Map — reinterpreted); reword the exhaustiveness claim as file-granular and state that any subsection not listed applies unchanged; place localization-§1-§4 under 'Does not apply' explicitly. The executable-content row (~:703) states ONE trigger: lint/testing/automated-tests are re-read when the repo tracks its first .lua file; any other executable content (a shell or Python script, a non-Lua test harness) MUST instead record in DEPENDENCIES.md how it is verified. Remove the three-trigger sentence. (Ruling: lint/testing/automated-tests presuppose Lua; this keeps dev-copilot's Python helpers and this repo's WS-10 shell script out of the Lua suites while still requiring a recorded verification.)
- LK-A-10 + WAS-R-06 (library-stack.md:223): split the mislabeled row into 'documentation-§5 | Keeping docs in sync.' and 'documentation-§6 | The filename-§N citation scheme and its citation rules.' so the §4 row's 'already named' cross-reference (~:261) holds; add the same 'any subsection not listed applies unchanged; the lists are file-granular' sentence to library-stack-§7's exhaustiveness paragraph (~:205). AUDIT.md:994 'documentation-§5/§6' -> 'documentation-§6'.
- WAS-A-16: in CLAUDE.md (~:155-156) and standards/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md:38, the Tier 2 parenthetical notes that perf-analysis/README.md is also a Tier 2 member, its trigger stated under verification-and-record.
- Changelog bullet appended to v2.77.0.

items.title: documentation-§6 gains a cross-repo citation SHOULD (symbol/heading for present tense, Repo@sha:path:line for history); convert the rotted citations and misleading counts to it
items.spec:
- New SHOULD in documentation-§6 (after the citation-scheme rules): a claim about another repo's code cites, in present tense, `Repo path` plus a symbol or heading (never a bare line number); a historical claim pins the commit, `Repo@<sha>:path:line`. A present-tense count or inventory is written as a rule ('every addon ...') or dated ('as measured on 2026-10-07'). Rationale: 43 of 61 cross-repo citations had moved and 6 named missing files (docs/audits/2026-10-07/03_EVIDENCE.md E5).
- Convert every citation in that E5 table that no longer matches (the 43 moved + 6 gone) — e.g. options-ui.md:410, standalone-windows.md:31/:34/:37, documentation.md:392-393/:416-418, library-stack.md:382-388 — to symbol/heading form or SHA-pin it; past-tense or delete the 6 gone claims (MultiMeters/settings/Schema.lua:1553-1566 in a 1392-line file; 'Five addons ship a private core/LSMPatch.lua' — none does).
- WAS-A-10: AUDIT.md:522-523 and standalone-windows.md:34 cite BankLedger 'B:MakeCloseButton' (modules/Browser.lua) by symbol, not :98.
- WAS-A-11 (no full recount): layout.md:93 PrettyChat splitter is tools/split_globalstrings.py — retire it as a known instance; EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY 'all eleven addons wrote' vs 'nine of nine' made consistent; EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md:52 'the eight addons' CRLF -> 'every addon in ADDONS.md'; other present-tense counts at audit-review-history.md:9/:11/:25/:51, AUDIT.md:145-146/:270/:343-348, documentation.md:150/:297-305/:359 ('Ten addons ship the re-vendor store'), library-stack.md:95, open-evolutions.md:71, options-ui.md:376/:408 reworded as rules or dated; history files get date stamps only.
- WAS-R-09: testing.md:292 'revision 24 ships today' -> 'LibKa0s test-kit revision 24 and later ship this'; testing.md:20 and NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md:1019 describe tests/_kit/ as 'vendored whole from LibKa0s testkit/, never edited' instead of a 4-of-22 file list.
- LK-A-08: library-stack.md:118 (Inter-module dependencies) cites the Options->Pool floor by symbol (the NEEDS_POOL floor) and names all three attach files: OptionsWidgets.lua, OptionsTabs.lua and OptionsNav.lua (no line numbers).
- Changelog bullet appended to v2.77.0.

items.title: versioning-git: default-branch work by default, owner-directed or multi-repo changesets on a same-named feat/<date>-<topic> branch merged --no-ff; ripple to the index blurb, context pack, anti-pattern #21, documentation-§8 and CLAUDE.md
items.spec:
Ruling (cluster C32): the trunk-based MUST is revised to match how the collection actually works; no per-repo deviation rows are filed (DC-A-12 becomes moot).
- standards/standards/versioning-git.md:13 replaced by: work lands on the repo's default branch by default; a changeset the owner directs to be isolated, or one that spans several repos, goes on feat/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<topic>, the SAME name in every repo it touches, merged into the default branch with --no-ff and then deleted (branch, and any worktree or stash the run created). Merging, tagging, pushing and releasing keep their owner go-ahead gates (the existing 'MUST NOT push unless the human asks' stays, with 'push a feature branch at a checkpoint the owner authorized' as the sanctioned case). Use repo-kind-neutral wording ('the repo's default branch', not 'the addon's') because documentation-§8 and library-stack-§7 bind this section to all three kinds.

- Changelog bullet appended to v2.77.0.

2. Apply the ripple sites listed; grep -i trunk across live docs.
3. Changelog bullet; commit.

items.title: Kit revision 38: Kit.secret, a shared secret-value simulator and an opt-in issecretvalue installer
items.spec: New testkit/secrets.lua returning function(Kit), loaded once from testkit/framework.lua beside asserts.lua/inventory.lua through kitFolder() (one load line; framework.lua stays under 1000 lines). Additive surface, all on Kit: Kit.secret(v) returns a wrapper table whose metatable raises an error whose message carries the fixed marker `secret value` (published as Kit.SECRET_ERROR) from __lt, __le, __add, __sub, __mul, __div, __mod, __pow, __unm, __concat, __len, __index, __newindex and __call, and from __eq when compared with another wrapper; Kit.isSecret(v) -> boolean; Kit.reveal(v) -> the plain value (identity for a non-secret); Kit.installSecretValue() sets the global issecretvalue to a function answering Kit.isSecret(v) and returns a restore function that puts back whatever global was there (nil included). The registry is one process-wide weak-keyed table so secrets minted under one mock build stay recognized under the next. Nothing installs issecretvalue by default: mock_base.lua's build is untouched, so no consumer's behaviour changes on re-vendor (fidelity: a client without the global stays modelled). The file header states plainly what Lua 5.1 cannot trap: a boolean test (`if s then`) and `==` against a non-table always succeed, and tostring(s) is not trapped; a test that needs those must assert them explicitly. No consumer local mock is migrated in this run (MultiMeters' tests/mock_secrets.lua models more); WhatGroup (WG-R-02) adopts it after the re-vendor. Kit stays at revision 38 (bumped by LK-01, unreleased): extend docs/api/testkit/version-38-docs.md with the new members (Since 38) and testkit/README.md's file inventory with secrets.lua. New suite tests/test_kit_secrets.lua added to tests/run.lua's SUITES (the suite inventory gate asserts it). CHANGELOG v1.71.0 entry. `cp -r testkit/. tests/_kit/`.

items.spec: LibKa0s/WidgetsLineChart.lua, CHART_MINOR 2 -> 3 (Widgets key 12.1.4.2.1 -> 12.1.4.3.1). items.title: /am select and /am delete resolve a bare number by exact name before id, refuse a cross-match, '#N' always means id
items.spec: settings/Slash.lua findContainer (about :166-:184), used by `select` and `delete`. New precedence: (a) arg trimmed; empty -> nil. (b) `#N` (N digits) always resolves as id N via NS.Database.FindContainer(N), never as a name. (c) Otherwise collect the exact case-insensitive name matches (as today; two or more -> the existing 'More than one container is called' refusal). (d) If arg is numeric (tonumber) AND a container named arg exists AND FindContainer(tonumber(arg)) is a DIFFERENT container, return nil plus a new enUS ambiguity sentence naming both, e.g. L["'%s' is both container #%s's name and container #%s's number — use #%s for the number"] (exact wording the implementer's, one locale key, enUS.lua only, formatted by the caller like the existing refusal). (e) Name match found -> it. (f) Numeric with no name match -> FindContainer(id) as today. Same container answering both name and id -> that container. The validator keeps accepting numeric names (forbidding them was rejected). The destructive delete path therefore never removes a container other than the one the player named. docs/slash-dispatch.md rows 12 (`select`) and 14 (`delete`) document the precedence; the `/am delete` help row (Slash.lua:70) and 'No such container' text stay unless the new `#N` form needs mentioning (add '#id' to the delete/select help text only if it fits the row shape).

Red first in tests/test_slash_verbs.lua: four cases — container named '3' plus a different container with id 3: `/am delete 3` refuses with the ambiguity line and deletes nothing; `/am delete #3` deletes id 3; a container named '7' with no id 7: `/am select 7` selects it by name; a numeric arg matching only an id still resolves by id. Add `-- red under:` notes; run and see them fail.
2. Implement the precedence in findContainer; add the enUS key.

4. regenerate docs/test-cases.md with `lua tests/run.lua --list > docs/test-cases.md` and roll the README Tests badge to the new Total in the same commit.

items.title: Macro fingerprint is trusted only when the live account-wide macro still holds that body; deleted or overwritten KCM_* macros are rewritten
items.spec: modules/MacroManager.lua. New local `liveBody(macroName)`: `local idx = GetMacroIndexByName and GetMacroIndexByName(macroName)`; returns nil when idx is nil or 0, else the body from `GetMacroInfo(idx)` (third return); both are unprotected reads and are safe in combat. `alreadyApplied(state, pending, body, icon)` gains the macro name and returns true only when the fingerprint matches (state.lastBody == body and state.lastIcon == icon) AND `liveBody(macroName) == body` AND (pending == nil or pending.body == body). On a missing macro or a live body that differs (another profile/character wrote its own body to the account-wide macro, or the player deleted it), commitMacro falls through to the existing path: queueForCombat in combat, else doEdit (which creates a missing macro) and the macroState store. Do not compare the live icon (GetMacroInfo returns a texture, not the stored icon key). No change to macroState's shape, to InvalidateState or MarkAllStale. items.title: Cast-bar name truncation counts UTF-8 characters, not bytes
items.spec: Option B (verdict): modules/Castbar.lua gains a file-local utf8Prefix(s, cap) mirroring MultiMeters/modules/Row_NameCell.lua utf8Truncate (walk bytes, count every byte outside 0x80-0xBF as a character start, return s:sub(1, i-1) at the (cap+1)th start, else s). truncateName (:335) keeps its nil/0/secret short-circuits, then: local cut = utf8Prefix(name, maxChars); if cut == name return name; else return cut .. items.title: /kcd debug: an unknown word refuses without toggling the console; castbar and interrupt take an optional target|focus unit
items.spec: core/KickCD.lua. (1) Split the sub-verb list printer out of runDebug's bare branch into a file-local printDebugList(self) (prints 'debug subcommands' plus NS.Slash.CommandRows('/kcd debug', DEBUG_COMMANDS, '  ')). The bare `/kcd debug` keeps its sanctioned behaviour (toggle the console, debug-logging-§5, then printDebugList). The unknown-word path becomes refuse(...) then printDebugList(self): it no longer re-enters runDebug(self, '') so it never toggles the console. (2) runDebug passes the remainder after the sub-verb to the handler: entry[3](self, remainder). A file-local parseDebugUnit(word) accepts '' -> 'target', 'target', 'focus' (case-insensitive) and returns nil otherwise. The castbar row calls m:DebugDump(unit) and the interrupt row NS.Compat.DebugInterrupt(unit); an unrecognized unit word refuses ('unknown unit '<w>', expected target or focus') through the existing refuse helper and runs nothing. Help strings: 'Print a unit's cast bar state (target by default, or focus)' and the interrupt row likewise names '[target|focus]'. Other rows ignore the remainder. runDebug stays at CCN <= 15. (3) Docs: docs/debug.md '/kcd debug castbar' (:277) and '/kcd debug interrupt' (:290) sections show the optional unit, docs/slash-dispatch.md's debug rows and README's command list if it names these verbs. Standard basis: slash-commands and debug-logging-§5 already sanction both the bare toggle and a usage reply.

items.title: Merge pets: an owner's own figures add to a cell its pet created earlier in the column instead of replacing it
items.spec:
Bug (high, must). modules/Aggregator.lua: with Merge pets on (settings/Schema.lua:1247), foldPet's absent-cell branch (~:265-273) creates the owner's cell from the pet's figures via setCell; when the owner's own source arrives later in the same column, placeSource's own path (~:927-928) calls setCell, which replaces row.values[statKey] outright (~:240), losing the pet's numbers. items.title: A partial roster is rebuilt at most once per aggregate pass, not on every lookup
items.spec:
modules/Roster.lua ensure() (~:537-541) returns build() whenever cache.partial is set, and Roster.Get / IsGroupMember / OwnerOf / LocalGUID all call ensure(), so one 7-column Aggregator.Build over a 3-member group with one unresolved unit costs ~60 UnitGUID calls instead of 3, every 0.25 s while the roster stays partial. The comments at :405 and :535 claim one walk per refresh.
End state:
- New public Roster.BeginPass(): arms exactly one retry of a partial roster (e.g. cache.retryArmed = true). ensure() rebuilds when there is no cache.group, or when cache.partial AND the retry is armed; build() disarms. A complete roster is never rebuilt by ensure() (unchanged). Invalidation paths (Roster.Refresh, Roster.Forget, GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE handling) keep their current behaviour.
- modules/Aggregator.lua Build calls Roster.BeginPass() once at the start of the pass, before any lookup, so every later lookup in that pass answers from cache. Callers outside a pass (tooltip, drill-down) read the cache.
- The comments at Roster.lua:405 and :535 say what the code now does (one retry per aggregate pass); the DebugSteady partial-line gating is unchanged.
- tests/test_roster.lua (or test_aggregator.lua): a case that counts UnitGUID calls (or build() runs) during one multi-column Aggregator.Build over a partial roster and asserts one rebuild for the pass (red: today it rebuilds per lookup); a case that a second pass retries again and a completed roster stops retrying. items.title: Stand-down drops combat-held unlocks so a later combat exit cannot unlock every panel
items.spec: modules/Unlock.lua: a new U:DropPending(reason) clears both `pendingUnlock` and `pendingPanels` (reuse dropAllUnlocks' held-request half, :245-:253, without touching NS.State.unlockedPanels), returns the number dropped, and writes one `[Unlock]` debug line when n > 0 ('dropped %d held unlock(s): %s'). core/LifecycleSetup.lua NS.StandDown (:101-:110) calls `NS.Unlock:DropPending('stood down')` (guarded on NS.Unlock) before unregistering PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED. While stood down, an unlock request is applied immediately instead of queued: U:SetUnlocked's combat branch is skipped when the addon is down (NS.IsAddonEnabled() false or the latch's down state), because there are no frames to hand the player and no REGEN event to replay it. Correct the core/LifecycleSetup.lua :65-:66 comment ('has nothing to defer while the addon is down') to say stand-down drops anything held. settings/Slash.lua:389 comment re-read for the same claim. U:ForgetPending is unchanged.

items.title: Non-Latin and accented panel names get distinct frame names; duplicate-name check folds UTF-8 case
items.spec: core/Util.lua Util.Slugify (:199-:203): ASCII alphanumerics are kept, runs of ASCII non-alphanumerics still collapse to one `_` (so 'Chat BG' and 'Chat-BG' still give 'Chat_BG' and every existing ASCII frame name is byte-identical), and every byte >= 0x80 is encoded as two upper-case hex digits (e.g. 'Ärger' -> 'C384rger', 'Обзор' -> 'D09ED0B1D0B7D0BED180'), so distinct UTF-8 names give distinct slugs. Encoded runs and ASCII text join without an extra separator; a name that is only ASCII punctuation still falls back to 'Panel'. Applies only where a frame name is derived for a NEW or re-stamped record (R:Create's Util.FrameName and the frameName backfill in R.Sanitize for records that have none); stored rec.frameName values are never rewritten, so existing anchors do not move. Duplicate-name guard independent of the slug: new Util.FoldName(name) = ASCII lower() plus a UTF-8 simple case fold for the Latin-1 Supplement (U+00C0-U+00DE except U+00D7 -> +0x20), Latin Extended-A even/odd pairs (U+0100-U+017F), Greek (U+0391-U+03A9 -> +0x20) and Cyrillic (U+0410-U+042F -> +0x20, U+0400-U+040F -> +0x50); R:FindByName (modules/Registry.lua:373-:381) compares FoldName on both sides, so 'Übersicht' and 'übersicht' are one name. Rewrite the Slugify comment (it relied on ASCII-only lower plus the slug collision). README.md:95-:99 ('anything that is not a letter or number turned into an underscore') gains one sentence: letters outside A-Z are written as hex codes, with an example. Keep modules/Registry.lua < 1000 lines (972 today) and core/Util.lua's functions <= CCN 15 (put the fold table in a local map). Reference PanelMaster#26 in the commit body. items.title: Panel number fields refuse NaN and infinity, and /pm recover repairs a non-finite position in one run
items.spec: One finite test, Util.IsFinite(n) in core/Util.lua: `type(n) == 'number' and n == n and n ~= math.huge and n ~= -math.huge`. Used in: settings/PanelSchema.lua COERCE.number (:40-:44) -> a non-finite tonumber result returns nil, 'expected a number' (so `/pm panel X set width nan|inf|-inf|1e999` is refused with the existing message); core/Util.lua Util.Clamp (:16-:22) -> a non-finite n falls back to tonumber(fallback) if finite, else lo; modules/Registry.lua freeNumber (:241) -> non-finite returns the template value; R:SetPosition (:811-:822) -> a non-finite x or y is dropped (as a non-number is today). R.RecoveredOffsets / R.IsOffScreen / R:Recover (:897-:930): a record whose x or y is non-finite is recovered to the clamped template offsets (0,0 within range), and IsOffScreen compares with the repaired value so a second /pm recover reports 0 moved (today NaN ~= NaN reports 'moved 1 panel' forever). Width/height non-finite are covered by Clamp. This item does not depend on LK-05 (the library's ParseValue refusal); both guards stand. Registry.lua stays < 1000 lines. items.title: Secure-write queue: one raising deferred write no longer orphans the rest; unwrapFrame re-wrap guarded
items.spec: core/PartyFrameEnhanced.lua flushSecure (:92-106): snapshot both `pending` and `pendingOrder` and replace them with fresh empty tables BEFORE running anything; then for each key in the snapshot order run its closure through xpcall(fn, geterrorhandler()) so an error still reaches BugSack/the default handler and the loop continues; count successes and failures and debug-log 'flushed %d deferred write(s), %d raised'. Consequences that must hold: after a raise the queue is empty (PendingSecureCount()==0, PendingSecureKeys() empty), a later in-combat RunSecure on the raising key re-queues it (the `if not pending[key]` guard sees nil), and OnLeaveCombat (:264-267) and the stand-down path still reach NS.PublishVisibility() after the flush. PFE-R-03: modules/SecureFollow.lua unwrapFrame (:193-201): the restoring SecureHandlerWrapScript(frame, SCRIPT, h, pre, post) runs through xpcall(..., geterrorhandler()) (never a bare pcall that discards the error) so the unwrap pass continues, consistent with Wrap's own guard (~:173); return false either way. PFE-R-05: settings/Slash.lua PROFILE_VERBS.new (:309-317): remove NS.ResetProfileCounted(db) after db:SetProfile(name) (the exists() refusal already guarantees a default-only profile) and rewrite the comment above it, which says 'SetProfile first, then the reset'; keep the exists() refusal and the 'Created and switched' line. Update docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (secure queue notes) and docs/slash-dispatch.md/docs/profiles.md wherever they describe the reset step.
